input.command:
python -c "
import pandas as pd,numpy as np
from lmfit.models import LorentzianModel,LinearModel
d=pd.read_csv('spectrum.csv');x=d.shift_cm1.values;y=d.intensity.values
for c,w in[(521,25),(1396.7,40)]:
    m=(abs(x-c)<w);mod=LorentzianModel()+LinearModel()
    p=mod.make_params(amplitude=1e4,center=c,sigma=5,slope=0,intercept=1000)
    r=mod.fit(y[m],p,x=x[m]);print(c,{k:(round(v.value,2),round(v.stderr or 0,2)) for k,v in r.params.items()}, 'fwhm',2*r.params['sigma'].value)
    print(x[m][np.argmax(y[m])])
print(np.std(y[(x>1450)&(x<1550)]))
# other narrow candidates: smoothed
from scipy.ndimage import uniform_filter1d
s=uniform_filter1d(y,5)
for lo,hi in[(60,300),(1580,1600),(2600,2800)]:
    m=(x>lo)&(x<hi);print(lo,hi,x[m][np.argmax(s[m])],s[m].max(),np.median(y[m]))
print(x[np.argsort(y)[-6:]],np.sort(y)[-6:])
"

peaks.assignment: hBN E2g (in-plane B-N stretch, high-frequency mode)
peaks.source: Lorentzian fit (centre 1396.49 +/- 0.02, FWHM 4.31 +/- 0.07). Assignment follows the hBN E2g literature: Geick 1966; Reich 2005; Vuong et al., Nature Mater. 2018 for isotope-dependent E2g. The polarization pattern is inferred from E2g symmetry in backscattering and not measured, since this is a single spectrum.
Lorentzian fit; first-order Si zone-centre phonon at 520.7 cm-1 (SiO2/Si substrate). The fitted centre agrees with the reference to better than 0.1 cm-1.

properties.name: Layer number / thickness
properties.value: Not determined. The strong E2g signal relative to Si suggests a multilayer or bulk-like flake, but there is no low-frequency shear mode (~52 cm-1 in bulk hBN) in the 60-1596 cm-1 window to confirm the layer count.
properties.source: Intensity ratio of E2g to Si

properties.name: Isotopic composition
properties.value: E2g at 1396.5 cm-1 is consistent with strong 10B enrichment (h-10BN). The enrichment fraction is not quantified.
properties.source: Vuong et al., Nature Mater. 17, 2018: E2g about 1393 cm-1 for h-10BN versus about 1356 for h-11BN and about 1366 for natural hBN

properties.name: E2g linewidth
properties.value: 4.3 cm-1 FWHM, a narrow line indicating good crystallinity. Isotopically pure hBN is expected to be narrower than natural hBN (~7-9 cm-1) because there is no isotopic disorder.

artifacts.type: Broad smooth background / fluorescence, strongest below ~300 cm-1 and decaying toward higher shift (about 2400 counts at 60-300 cm-1 versus about 650 at 1500 cm-1)
No cosmic-ray spikes identified; all prominent features are either the two fitted peaks or noise (~66 counts rms).

Reich et al., Phys. Rev. B 71, 205201 (2005): Raman of hBN, E2g at about 1366 cm-1
Vuong et al., Nature Mater. 17, 152 (2018): isotopically enriched h-10BN and h-11BN, E2g isotope shift
Temple & Hathaway, Phys. Rev. B 7, 3685 (1973): Si first-order line at 520.7 cm-1
limits: The assignment rests on one band, so identification is not unique. The ~1396 cm-1 position is ~30 cm-1 above natural hBN and matches isotope-enriched h-10BN only by comparison with literature values. An independent check by isotope-sensitive methods or by composition would be needed.
The E2g mode of h-10BN is reported at about 1393-1394 cm-1, so the observed 1396.5 cm-1 is slightly higher, possibly because of strain or partial enrichment. This is not resolved by these data.
Layer number cannot be determined. There is no resolvable low-frequency shear mode in the 60-1596 cm-1 range, and the E2g position and width are not a reliable thickness gauge here.
Polarization dependence cannot be measured from a single unpolarized-analysis spectrum. The 'isotropic_both' label comes from E2g symmetry in backscattering, not from data.
The spectrum stops at 1596 cm-1, so any bands above that are not covered.
The broad background below ~300 cm-1 could not be attributed (substrate, fluorescence, or Rayleigh tail) and no weak sample bands were resolved above the noise.
